general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.

F1 Spans are short, mostly one or two words. Label the core term without the modifiers before it or the noun after it: "fatigue" in "high-cycle fatigue resistance", "oxygen" in "dissolved oxygen", "tungsten" and "rod" in "tungsten rod".

classes.name: EngineeringFeatures
classes.description: Encompass distinct terms or phrases that convey specific information related to the structural, functional, or visual properties of a manufacturing process.

classes.name: ProcessParameters
classes.description: Process parameters refer to specific quantitative values or attributes that play a significant role in manufacturing processes.

classes.name: EnablingTechnology
classes.description: Specific tools, methods, processes, or technologies that play a pivotal role in facilitating or enhancing various aspects of manufacturing processes.
rules: ET1 "rapid prototyping" and "generative design" are EnablingTechnology, not ManufacturingProcess.

classes.name: Material
classes.description: Refers to any substance or compound used in manufacturing processes that has a significant impact on the process, properties, or characteristics of the end product.
rules: MA1 Materials can include metals, alloys, polymers, ceramics, composites, and more.

MA2 A Material span is the material name alone, without grade numbers, modifiers or the part made of it: "metal" in "metal parts", "carbon steel" in "carbon steel cladding", "metallic glass" in "bulk metallic glass", "Ti" in "Ti 6-4".

classes.name: MechanicalProperties
classes.description: Refers to specific attributes or characteristics of materials that describe their behavior under mechanical forces and conditions.
rules: MEC1 These properties play a crucial role in manufacturing processes and are often used to evaluate the suitability and performance of materials for different applications.
MEC2 Named properties and defects stay MechanicalProperties: "tensile properties", "porosity", "residual stress", "anisotropy", "pores", "ductility".

classes.name: ManufacturingStandards
classes.description: Refer to specific guidelines, specifications, benchmarks, and terminology used within the manufacturing industry to ensure uniformity, quality, and compatibility of products, processes, and systems.

classes.name: ManufacturingProcess
classes.description: Refers to a specific technique, method, or procedure used in the production of goods.
rules: MP1 A process span leaves out modifiers and the product: "arc welding" in "robotic arc welding", "sand casting" in "green sand casting", "additively manufactured" in "additively manufactured components".
MP2 After "AM" the next noun stays in the span: "AM process", "AM processes" and "AM technologies" are ManufacturingProcess.

classes.name: Application
classes.description: Refers to the specific field or industry in which a manufacturing process is utilized or intended to be utilized.
rules: AP1 It signifies the purpose, domain, or sector where the manufacturing process finds its use.

classes.name: MachineEquipment
classes.description: Any necessary items required for a particular purpose, including assembled parts and set of tools.
rules: ME1 Equipments are required to set up not only the mechanical machines, but also for setting up any relevant operation or task.
ME2 "AM parts", "AM machines", "3D printers" and "3D printer" are MachineEquipment, not ManufacturingProcess.

classes.name: ConceptPrinciples
classes.description: Refers to key concepts, principles, and elements related to manufacturing processes.
rules: CP1 "mechanical properties", "microhardness", "microstructure", "HAZ" and "heat affected zone" are ConceptPrinciples, not MechanicalProperties.
CP4 "geometry" and "interface" are ConceptPrinciples, not EngineeringFeatures.
CP6 "process parameters" is ConceptPrinciples, not ProcessParameters.

classes.name: ProcessCharacterization
classes.description: Refers to the detailed analysis and measurement of various aspects of manufacturing processes to understand their performance, quality, and characteristics.
rules: PC1 Microscopy, diffraction and test methods are ProcessCharacterization, not EnablingTechnology: "scanning electron microscopy", "EBSD", "X-ray diffraction", "tensile tests".

classes.name: Biomedical
classes.description: Refers to any biomedical entity involved in the manufacturing process.
